title: Discoid lupus erythematosus
summary: Chronic cutaneous lupus causing red, scaly plaques on the face, ears and scalp that scar, depigment and cause permanent hair loss. Strict photoprotection, potent steroids and early referral prevent disfigurement.

glance.think: Red, scaly, coin-shaped plaques on the face, ears or scalp that leave scarring, pigment change or bald patches.
glance.engine: Autoimmune interface dermatitis triggered by UV; smoking makes it worse and blunts hydroxychloroquine.
glance.backbone: Broad-spectrum sunscreen and sun avoidance, stop smoking, potent topical or intralesional steroid; specialist hydroxychloroquine.
glance.never_miss: Scarring alopecia, systemic lupus (screen symptoms and bloods), and SCC in long-standing scars.

what: **Discoid lupus erythematosus** is the most common form of **chronic cutaneous lupus**. Scarring inflammatory plaques favour head and neck; scalp disease causes **scarring alopecia**. Most patients have skin-limited disease, but a minority evolve toward systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Module 4 Formative Quiz-1 answer was DLE (vs alopecia areata, LPP, tinea capitis, trichotillomania).

list: Autoimmune interface dermatitis with follicular involvement.

Risk factors emphasised in teaching: **darker skin phototypes** have higher rates of DLE and more disfiguring dyspigmentation/scarring; smoking associated with DLE activity/treatment resistance; female predominance overall (quiz noted male sex is *not* the higher-risk factor).

head: Feature
Detail
rows: Well-defined erythematous discs; adherent scale; follicular plugging; “carpet tack” scale when removed
Central atrophy, permanent hair loss on scalp, pigment change
Face, ears, scalp, neck; occasionally below neck
May burn/itch; cosmetic distress high (quiz vignette)

list: Clinical + **skin biopsy** (most important confirmatory test in quiz cluster).
Bloods: ANA, ENA, complement — useful to screen for systemic disease but **may be negative** in purely cutaneous DLE.
Mycology if tinea capitis plausible; trichoscopy helps vs AA/LPP.

head: Look-alike
Distinguishing clues
rows: Non-scarring; exclamation hairs; no discoid scale plaques
Scarring; perifollicular scale; less classic facial discoid plaques
Bizarre geometric; hairs of different lengths

list: Potent/very potent TCS or intralesional steroid (often derm); topical calcineurin inhibitors on face sometimes.
Early derm referral for scalp/face to minimise irreversible scarring.
Screen for SLE symptoms (arthritis, serositis, renal, photosensitivity beyond skin, cytopenias).

red_flags: Joint pain, mouth ulcers, fatigue, chest pain or Raynaud’s: screen for **SLE** (ANA, FBC, urine dipstick) and refer.
Scalp DLE with hair loss: **urgent** dermatology (scarring alopecia).
Hydroxychloroquine: baseline and annual eye screening after 5 years (RCOphth).
pearls: Emphasise scarring risk — early treatment matters.
Camouflage / psychological support for visible disease.
Check BNF interactions if hydroxychloroquine co-prescribed later (retinopathy monitoring is specialty).

references.label: RCOphth: Hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine retinopathy screening
